title: KV hotspot sampling, adaptive version safety-net, and profile publish workflow
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Goal: Implement an automated workflow that (1) identifies per-model KV 'hotspots' and tail-sequence patterns via lightweight sampling, (2) computes a conservative version-safety net for pinning that allows safe rollforward when new runtime/kernel versions are released, and (3) publishes validated performance profiles and a deterministic manifest to the model catalog so Dedicated/Private can consume them.

Motivation: Current onboarding relies on heavy offline profiling or broad heuristics that either miss sequence-tail behaviors or over-pin to older kv profiles, causing unnecessary evictions and increased latency for long-context requests. We need a reproducible pipeline that balances safety (no quality regressions) with deploy agility (ability to accept safe runtime kernels and quantized variants).

Scope and deliverables:
- Sampling agent that runs on a small percentage of production traffic (0.1-1%) to collect KV access patterns, sequence-tail spike events, and latency histograms per model and route.
- Hotspot detector that groups sequences into clusters (short, mid, tail) and emits a compact signature for each cluster: avg.seq_len_quantile, top-k KV reuse ratio, and tail-frequency metric.
- Safety-net generator that proposes a minimal pin range (model version + runtime/quantization variants) that has historically matched the signature and meets latency/regression thresholds. This generator must be conservative by default and expose a tuning knob per customer tier.
- Rollforward policy implementation: automated canary that applies new kernel/runtime variants only if the cached signature match rate is >= 95% and percentiles p90/p99 latency regression < 5% against baseline. If checks fail, automatically pin to safety-net and create a publish artifact with rationale.
- Profile publishing pipeline: validated binary profile + JSON manifest (version, signature hashes, sampling window, telemetry checks, golden prompts used for regression tests) published to the model catalog and surfaced in console under "KV Profiles".
- CI/validation harness: unit tests, simulated workload replay (from golden traces), and an E2E smoke job that runs on staging Dedicated cluster.

Acceptance criteria:
- Sampling agent deployed behind feature flag and collecting signatures at 0.5% traffic with <1ms added p50 latency overhead in controlled canary.
- Hotspot detector produces stable signatures for 95% of models in the first 7 days of sampling.
- Safety-net generator provides pin ranges and rollforward recommendations for onboarded models; experimentation shows <2% false positives where a suggested pin caused user-visible regression.
- Profile publish artifacts are generated and uploaded to catalog with unique content-hash and can be consumed by Dedicated and Private deployments via existing manifest endpoint.
- Console UI shows new profile metadata and a link to the golden-requests regression run per profile.

Out of scope: full automated eviction of KV entries, deep offline sequence clustering jobs (>24h), and model-retraining-triggered changes.

Risks and mitigation:
- Sampling bias: mitigate by rotating sampling windows across regions and request routes.
- Data volume: store only compact signatures and aggregate histograms; raw traces retained only for 7 days.
- Safety false negatives: conservative thresholds and manual review gate for high-traffic models.
